title: BatchZK: A Fully Pipelined GPU-Accelerated System for Batch Generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
problem: GPU-accelerated zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) systems optimize for low single-proof latency but do not support high-throughput batch proof generation, creating a bottleneck for applications like blockchain and verifiable ML that require generating many proofs concurrently.
motivation: The explosive growth of ZKP applications in blockchain and verifiable ML demands high-throughput batch proof generation, which existing single-proof-optimized GPU systems cannot efficiently provide.
method: BatchZK constructs a fully pipelined GPU execution engine for batch ZKP generation. The pipeline overlaps the multiple stages of proof generation (e.g., polynomial commitment, multi-scalar multiplication, NTT) across multiple concurrent proofs using GPU streams and memory management strategies that keep GPU compute units busy throughout. By co-scheduling proofs at different stages simultaneously on the GPU, BatchZK amortizes memory transfer and kernel launch overhead across the batch, maximizing GPU throughput. The system targets standard ZKP schemes (e.g., Groth16 or PLONK-family) that underpin modern blockchain applications.
key_novelty: Full pipeline parallelism across independent ZKP generation tasks on GPU, turning the sequential single-proof flow into a throughput-optimized batch pipeline for the first time.
contributions: Fully pipelined GPU execution framework for batch ZKP generation
Overlap of polynomial commitment, MSM, and NTT stages across concurrent proofs via GPU streams
Throughput-optimized batch scheduling that amortizes GPU overhead across proofs
Demonstrated high-throughput batch proof generation for blockchain/verifiable ML applications

metrics.other: throughput improvement over single-proof GPU systems (not quantified in abstract)

limitations: Batch size and pipeline depth tradeoffs under variable proof sizes or ZKP scheme variants are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Pipelined GPU batch zero-knowledge proof generation
